answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut is the binding constraint and the 14-day expiration forces a decision. Memory c2 documents that the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — the only direction that simultaneously addresses the finance mandate and the imminent contract expiry. Memory c6 (multi-year incumbent pricing) is checked as a counterfactual because a multi-year extension might also lower unit cost, but the primary objective is total cost of ownership under a hard 18% target; the incumbent's locked-in structure is less likely to reach that depth of cut without a fresh competitive benchmark, and the contract does not auto-renew, so inaction is not an option. Delivery risk is managed by the fact that c2 confirmed stable invoicing and fast integration last year; the assembly line at 94% with no buffer means I cannot afford a mis-transition, but the prior onboarding was quick. Add_second_source and defer_decision do not move the cost needle enough in one cycle, and negotiate_terms alone is unlikely to hit 18% with the incumbent.
